reuse.why: Extends the existing shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend and passes holidays through every existing caller, though the window widening is not routed through the new getWeekendSearchWindow helper outside shared/schedules.ts.

duplication.why: The 'widen the occurrence window for holidays' concern is written three times with three different formulas (getWeekendSearchWindow, count*7 + holidays*7 in getUpcomingDates, 2*(holidays+1) in getDatesInRange), and holidays is threaded by hand into four call sites that each keep their own skipWeekend ternary.

placement.why: The holiday-as-weekend rule lives in the shared date-adjust function in shared/schedules.ts, with the type added to RecurConfig and parsing in rule-utils, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Only schedule date handling, its type, parsing, and focused tests are touched.

maintainability.why: The rewritten stepping loop is clear and general; the scattered ad hoc window-size formulas are the part a maintainer would want unified.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All date-adjust paths call getDateWithSkippedWeekend; none re-implements the weekend/holiday rule.

disguised_duplication.where: Window sizing for holidays: getWeekendSearchWindow in shared/schedules.ts vs inline count*7 + holidays.length*7 in getUpcomingDates and shiftDays = 2*(holidays.length+1) in getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) express the same concern in reshaped forms.

one_place.where: The rule 'a holiday is treated like a weekend day' is defined once in isWeekendOrHoliday/getDateWithSkippedWeekend (shared/schedules.ts) and every path (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, schedule-template getAdjustedDate) applies it through that function; only the search-window sizing is spread out.
